messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: prod - increased 5xx rate on /v1/generate (canary rollout). Alerting oncall. Details: Canary group 'canary-a' -> 12% 5xx vs baseline 0.3%. Rolling window 5m.

alex: acked — taking lead. Any customer-impact notes?

incident-bot: Affected subset: ~4% of production traffic routed to canary-a. Error trace shows image digest mismatch during container startup (manifest mismatched).

maria: I can look at the pods. `kubectl -n prod get pods -l rollout=canary-a` shows CrashLoopBackOff on 3/12 replicas. Logs: `error: failed to open token: manifest digest not found for tag canary-2026-04-01`

jamal: Paging CI team — did we push a bad manifest? @maria can you paste the image reference from a failing pod?

maria: From pod: `Image: registry.redwood-inference.com/serving:canary-2026-04-01@sha256:deadbeef` but registry GET for that digest returns a different manifest (points to a lightweight shim). Looks like tag -> digest mapping is inconsistent.

sophia: This smells like the publish-manifest job in Buildkite might have used cached blobs. We had a runner restart during the publish step earlier. Could be cache poisoning where the tag got re-pointed to the wrong digest.

alex: Impact assessment: customers hitting canary routes only; still low percentage but 5xx spikes. Recommend immediate rollback of canary + flip feature flag kill-switch.

ops-qa: Agreed. Recommend: 1) flip feature flag `enable_canary_routing` -> false, 2) rollback deployment to previous stable revision, 3) block the bad tag in registry and re-publish correct manifest.

alex: Doing the flag flip now. `curl -X POST https://flags.redwood-infra.local/flags/enable_canary_routing -d '{"value":false}'` -> 200 OK :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Flag update received. Propagating to edge routers (approx 10s).

maria: Starting rollback: `kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/serving --to-revision=128`

deploy-bot: Rollout undo initiated. Current rollout status:
```
NAME      READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE   AGE
serving   12/12   12           12          3m
```
Rollout completing...

jamal: Can someone open the registry and mark `canary-2026-04-01` as quarantined? I don't want anyone else pulling it accidentally.

maria: Quarantined the tag in our internal registry UI and added a redirect rule to return 404 for that tag. Added note: "Do not re-use until investigation completes."

sophia: I'm checking Buildkite job `publish-manifest` logs. There's a `sccache` failure around 11:23 UTC where the runner crashed and restarted. The artifact publish step retried and seems to have re-uploaded a different manifest under the same tag. The job had `--force` tagging enabled.

jamal: That's our root cause then — transient runner restart + force-tag + shared tag -> cache poisoning. We need an immediate mitigation in CI to stop `--force` tag on publish and ensure we push by digest and then tag immutably.

alex: For customers: ops-qa, please draft a short status (internal + customer-facing) stating limited impact, canary only, rollback done, investigating root cause.

ops-qa: Drafting now. Customers impacted: "Some requests to /v1/generate may have experienced 5xx errors between 11:20-11:48 UTC. A canary rollout is being rolled back; stable traffic unaffected. We will follow up with RCA."

maria: Post-rollback checks: health checks passing across all regions, error rate back to baseline within ~3 minutes after flag flip.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed. Old revision 128 is now active.

jamal: Next steps for remediation (assigned):
- Disable `--force` tag in publish job (PR queued) — jamal
- Add immutable tag policy + registry pre-publish digest verify — maria
- Add CI step: verify manifest digest matches release artifact before tagging — sophia
- Run registry sweep to find other tags with mismatched digests — ops-qa

alex: I'm handing off to the next oncall now. Summary for handoff: canary rollout caused 5xx due to tag->digest mismatch from CI publish after runner restart. Mitigation: flipped canary flag, rolled back deployment to revision 128, quarantined bad tag, customers largely unaffected (canary only). Follow-ups assigned.

incident-bot: Handoff: oncall->oncall-next at 11:55 UTC. Incident severity: sev2 -> monitoring for escalation.

sophia: I've raised PR #402 to add digest verification and to forbid `--force` unless explicitly approved in release notes. Please review.

jamal: Also adding a buildkite check to fail the publish if runner restart was detected in the last 2 minutes (makes retries require human confirmation).

ops-qa: Saving logs/artifacts to the incident bucket: `s3://incidents/1841004321/` — includes failing pod logs, publish-manifest logs, registry snapshot.

alex: Thanks team. I'll follow up in the morning with a short RCA draft. Leaving a note for next oncall: please confirm registry sweep and PR reviews, and escalate to security if you find any image with mismatched content beyond this tag.

ops-qa: Acknowledged handoff.

maria: Last note — we observed ~2% user-facing error rate for affected customers during the window (rough estimate based on sampling).

jamal: Closing chat, switching to post-incident backlog tasks. :white_check_mark:
